cards.explanation: The answer is False. David says these men "…devise evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long." (Psalm 140:2). Not once in a while, but all day long. I think that's a heavy thing to read, friends.

The answer is snakes. David says they "…sharpen their tongues like snakes…" (Psalm 140:3). Then he adds that the venom of vipers is on their lips. A sharp tongue with venom on it is a hard picture, friends.

The word is stumble. These men of violence "…scheme to make me stumble." (Psalm 140:4). To scheme means it's planned, not an accident. I think David feels like somebody is out to trip him up, and he takes that straight to the LORD.

The answer is a snare and a net, friends. David says, "The proud hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set out for me." (Psalm 140:5). That's a trap on the very path he walks. Somebody did some serious planning.

The answer is True, friends. With a snare hidden and a net spread along his path, David says to the LORD, "You are my God." (Psalm 140:6). Then he adds, "Hear, O LORD, my cry for help." Even with all that along his path, he talks to the LORD anyway.

The answer is that the LORD shields his head. David says, "…You shield my head in the day of battle." (Psalm 140:7). He's talking to the LORD, whom he calls "…the strength of my salvation…" I'd take a shield over a hat any day, friends, and I own a very tall hat.

The answer is False, friends. David prays, "Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not promote their evil plans, lest they be exalted." (Psalm 140:8). He asks the LORD to say no to their plans. Some prayers are just a very sincere "please don't."

The answer is the trouble their own lips caused. David prays, "May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused." (Psalm 140:9). The trouble is what he asks to cover their heads, friends. It's trouble their own lips have caused.

The answer is that the LORD upholds justice for them! David says, "I know that the LORD upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy." (Psalm 140:12). Notice the words "I know," friends. After all those requests, he says what he's sure of. That's a good way to land a prayer.

The word is dwell, friends. "Surely the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence." (Psalm 140:13). To dwell means to live there, not just visit. David starts the psalm crying for rescue and ends it sure about that.
